title: Synthetic workload orchestrator spec
content:
Purpose:
- Design notes and quick spec for a lightweight, developer-first synthetic workload orchestrator.
- Goal: reproducible, parameterized traffic + failure injection for exercising routing, batching, KV/prefix cache, quantization variant fallbacks, and rollout policies.

High-level goals (what I want this to do):
- Compose rich traffic mixes (tenants, routes, model variants) with per-tenant SLAs.
- Inject targeted failures (region outage, increased latency, qps throttles, partial model unavailability).
- Drive realistic sequence-length and token-distribution profiles (not just uniform).
- Collect per-run metrics (p50/p95 latency per-route, token cost, fallback rate, batch sizes seen, cache-hit rates).
- Be scriptable from CI and interactive for local dev experiments.

Why this matters:
- We keep discovering subtle regressions after model/infra changes (e.g., batching changes cause higher p99s under skew). We need a way to synthesize those signals deterministically.
- Sandbox for policy experiments (routing by cost vs latency, canary config impact).

Core concepts / model:
- WorkloadProfile: describes a distribution over requests. Keys: tenant_mix, route_weights, model_variants, seq_len_dist, token_dist, warmup_behavior, concurrency
- FailureProfile: timed injections with scope (tenant/region/route/global). Types: latency_spike, drop_fraction, model_unavailable, kv_cache_eviction, gpu_outage.
- OrchestrationPlan: timeline of workload and failures. Repeatable seed (rng_seed).
- MetricsExport: predefined schema for run outputs (flat labels + numeric series).

Component sketch (controller + workers):
- controller (single, coordinates runs, exposes REST/CLI).
- driver-worker(s) (stateless processes that generate synthetic client calls to target Redwood endpoints).
- injector (integrated in controller or as sidecar) that calls platform control plane to simulate failure conditions (or talks to test harness hooks on dedicated infra).
- collector (pulls metrics via telemetry API + injects trace headers for distributed tracing).

Light ASCII diagram (very rough):

  +-----------------+      control      +--------------------+    telemetry   +-----------+
  | CLI / CI / UI   | --------------->  | Controller         |  ----------->  | Collector |
  +-----------------+                   +--------------------+                +-----------+
         |                                        |                                |
         | start run                              | spawn drivers                   | pull metrics & traces
         v                                        v                                v
  +-----------------+   synthetic streams   +-----------------+   calls  +--------------------+
  | local test/dev  | --------------------> | driver-worker   |------->  | Target runtime API  |
  +-----------------+                       +-----------------+          +--------------------+

API shapes (controller):
- POST /v1/runs/start  payload: (example YAML/JSON shown as text)  {
    "name": "canary-routing-latency-test",
    "rng_seed": 23421,
    "duration_s": 900,
    "profile": {
      "tenant_mix": [{"tenant": "shopA", "pct": 50}, {"tenant": "shopB", "pct": 30}, {"tenant": "guest", "pct": 20}],
      "route_weights": [{"route": "/v1/generate", "weight": 80}, {"route": "/v1/embeddings", "weight": 20}],
      "model_variants": [{"model": "redwood-2b-8k", "pct": 70}, {"model": "redwood-2b-8k-quant", "pct": 30}],
      "seq_len_dist": {"type": "mixed", "bins": [{"len": 64, "pct": 35}, {"len": 512, "pct": 50}, {"len": 2048, "pct": 15}]},
      "token_dist": {"avg": 120, "stddev": 80},
      "concurrency": {"targets": [{"clients": 200, "rps": 300}], "ramp": "linear:60s"}
    },
    "failure_profile": [{"at_s": 300, "type": "latency_spike", "scope": "region:us-west1", "params": {"extra_ms": 300}}, {"at_s": 540, "type": "model_unavailable", "scope": "model:redwood-2b-8k", "params": {"duration_s": 60}}]
  }

Notes: controller accepts YAML or JSON; rng_seed is important for reproducibility. "params" is freeform map in payload (we'll validate on controller).

Driver behavior (pseudocode):
- on start, fetch profile; for each synthetic client:
  - sample tenant according to tenant_mix
  - choose route via route_weights
  - choose model variant (and attach expected headers e.g. X-Model-Variant)
  - sample seq_len and token length, build prompt templates from corpus (we should store small corpuses per tenant)
  - perform requests at scheduled times to match RPS shape; optionally use multiplexing to simulate many logical clients from one worker process
  - annotate each request with run_id, rng_seed, client_id, and an internal seq to allow reassembly

Failure injection approaches (options):
- preferred: use test hooks on dedicated test deployment (control plane API to simulate region=degraded). Safer for production-like fidelity.
- alternative: network-level proxies that throttle or add latency on path between drivers and target (useful for offline dev).
- last-resort: mutate client headers or request body to trigger route-based fallbacks.

Observability contract (metrics to export):
- per-run, per-tenant, per-route: request_count, success_count, error_count, fallback_count, avg_tokens, token_cost, latency_p50/p90/p95/p99, batch_size_histogram, cache_hit_rate
- event timeline: failure events emitted with timestamp and scope
- traces: sampled traces should contain controller.run_id, driver.client_id, target_request_id, model_variant_on_entry, actual_model_serving_name

Example metrics CSV header (flat):
run_id,tenant,route,model_variant,timestamp,reqs,errors,p50_ms,p95_ms,avg_tokens,token_cost,batch_p50,cache_hit_pct

Quick CLI examples:
- start run: rwoctl run start --file canary.yaml --out run-233.json
- status: rwoctl run status --run run-233
- stop: rwoctl run stop --run run-233
- fetch metrics: rwoctl run fetch-metrics --run run-233 --format csv > run-233-metrics.csv

Local dev flow (notes to self):
- provide "local" mode that talks to a dev endpoint and sets failure injections via a per-test proxy (env var DEV_PROXY=...).
- include a small container that can serve as a fake target (returns configurable latencies, simulates kv cache misses) for offline iteration.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How heavy should driver-worker be? Single-threaded per process or multithreaded with async clients? Start simple: async single process with configurable concurrency.
- Integration with our telemetry ingestion: push vs pull? Prefer push for CI runs (controller pushes aggregated metrics at end) and pull for long-running experiments.
- Security: ensure run IDs and injected failures are scoped to test infra. We must avoid accidentally toggling prod deployment fallbacks. Add explicit allowlist for target endpoints.
- Corpus: build small per-tenant prompt corpuses (50-200 prompts) derived from anonymized logs. Where to store? S3 bucket or repo assets?
- CLI auth: integrate with existing Redwood creds and token scopes (rwoctl should get ephemeral test token).

Runbook checklist (when running a noisy test):
- confirm target endpoints are test/dev or dedicated capacity (no accidental prod hits)
- confirm allowlist and dry-run flag set
- collect run artifacts: controller log, driver logs, metrics export, example raw request traces (3-5), seed used
- post-run: run automated SLO assertions and upload results to confluence/test-results

Experiments I want to run first:
- 1) Small-scale routing canary: 100 clients, 60/40 model split, induce a short model_unavailable on primary variant and measure fallback rate & p99 impact
- 2) Batching sensitivity: run same RPS with different concurrency patterns to measure batch sizes and token_cost delta
- 3) KV cache thrash: simulate a cache-eviction window and measure token cost jump and latency impact

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Make controller idempotent. If runs fail mid-way we should be able to restart with same seed and pick up logs.
- Keep DSL intentionally small; implement transform to expand into driver-level events.
- Keep sample corpuses and short templates in repo under /test/fixtures/workloads.
- We should add a small UI in Console to replay saved runs and visualize per-route timelines (stretch).

References / quick links:
- JIRA-4821: workload harness epic (design + acceptance criteria)
- infra PR 256: lightweight dev proxy for latency injection
- confluence: synthetic-workloads (placeholder page)

If this doc survives first pass, next step: sketch minimal MVP API + tiny PoC driver (golang or python async) and a small pipeline to transform run artifacts into CSV and a Jupyter notebook for visualization.

-- Samira
